new_statements.quote: p. 70: "Mnogi kajkavski govori čuvaju još staru hrvatskosrpsku akcentuaciju sa 3 osnovna prahrvatskosrpska akcenta ̑ ̏ ̃, kako sam je ja već prije 25 godina uzimao (v. »Rad« 187, 207). Akcenat ̑ odgovara praslavenskom ̑ (u primjerima kao mȇso) i metatonijskom ̑ (u primjerima kao gen. pl. krȃvā); ̃ je po mome bilježenju t. zv. novi akut (u primjerima kao sũša); ̏ odgovara praslavenskom ̏ (u primjerima kao ȍko) i starom akutu (u primjerima kao krȁva)." — p. 73: "Konservativna grupa čuva više ili manje staru akcentuaciju, osobito mjesto starijega akcenta. U toj grupi možemo razlikovati dva pojasa, i to jedan s oksitonezom tipa ženȁ i drugi bez takve oksitoneze [...] Revolucionarna grupa karakterizirana je time, što se u njoj stara akcentuacija ne samo s obzirom na mjesto akcenta, nego i s obzirom na intonaciju više ili manje promijenila."
new_statements.translation: p. 70: "Many Kajkavian dialects still preserve the old Croato-Serbian accentuation with the 3 basic Proto-Croato-Serbian accents ̑ ̏ ̃, as I already assumed 25 years ago (see Rad 187, 207). The accent ̑ corresponds to Proto-Slavic ̑ (in examples like mȇso) and to the metatonic ̑ (in examples like gen. pl. krȃvā); ̃ is, in my notation, the so-called neo-acute (in examples like sũša); ̏ corresponds to Proto-Slavic ̏ (in examples like ȍko) and to the old acute (in examples like krȁva)." p. 73: "The conservative group preserves more or less the old accentuation, especially the place of the older accent. In this group we can distinguish two belts, one with oxytonesis of the type ženȁ and the other without such oxytonesis [...] The revolutionary group is characterised by the fact that in it the old accentuation has changed more or less not only with respect to the place of the accent but also with respect to intonation."

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Kajkavian has an empty rule; Ivšić supplies the substance: a free, lexically/morphologically placed three-tone pitch accent (ȁ ȃ ã) in the conservative dialects, with place shifts (metataxis) and tone changes (metatonia) in the eastern 'revolutionary' dialects and a weight-conditioned last-two-syllables rule in the Podravina subtype. Nothing in the catalog is contradicted.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kajkavian has a three-way tonal accent system (short falling ȁ, long falling/circumflex ȃ, long rising 'neo-acute' ã) with contrastive intonation and quantity; the place of accent is not fixed to a syllable position but inherited lexically and morphologically (e.g. oxytone ženȁ vs. initial lȉpa, gen. pl. krȃvā vs. nom. krȁva, prez. mȋsli). Ivšić divides the dialects into a conservative group (old place of accent kept, with or without final-syllable oxytonesis of the žena type) and a revolutionary group (place shifted by 'metataxis' toward the word-beginning or word-end, and intonation changed by 'metatonia'), further split into four main groups (I older Kajkavian, II Čakavian-Kajkavian, III younger Kajkavian with metataxis, IV younger Kajkavian with metatonia), pp. 80-81.
new_statements.exceptions: p. 84 (p. 39): the Podravina type IV7-8 (Bregi, Novigrad, Virje, Đurđevec etc.) has a positional rule: "u njemu može biti akcentovan samo posljednji ili pretposljednji slog, i to posljednji, ako je iskonski ili sekundarno kajkavski dug, a pretposljednji, ako je posljednji kratak" — only the last or the penultimate syllable may be accented: the last if it is (originally or secondarily) long, otherwise the penult (e.g. mlȋnar, čȗvam, kravȃr, ženȁ > žȅna). Ivšić calls this the most 'revolutionary' type and states it derives from the common Kajkavian base, not from any Bulgarian parallel (p. 85). p. 74: educated Kajkavian speakers usually replace the neo-acute ã by the long falling accent (pȋšem, čȗvam).
new_statements.identity_note: Ivšić describes Croatian Kajkavian as a whole (the dialects of 'Hrvati kajkavci' north-west of the Štokavian line), with a four-group accentual classification: I older Kajkavian (Zagorje–Međimurje, west of a Delekovec–Krapina–Sv. Ivan Zelina line), II Čakavian-Kajkavian (Zaprešić–Sutla–Sava corner, western Samobor, Žumberak, the Sava–Bregana ikavian pocket), III younger Kajkavian with metataxis (Turopolje–Posavina, south-east), IV younger Kajkavian with metatonia (Križevci–Podravina, north-east). The weight-sensitive last-two-syllables rule (p. 84) is specific to the Podravina subtype IV7-8 (Bregi, Novigrad, Virje, Đurđevec). The ikavian Kajkavian speakers of Brdovec/Marija Gorica (§12, pp. 74-78) are said to have their own accentuation of Čakavian origin.

tone_statements.translation: ...a complete analysis of Križanić's texts has made it possible to understand better the phonemic make-up of his dialect (Oslon 2012) and its prosodic inventory (two phonologically short tones and only one long one, see Oslon 2012: 74) ... [fn. 14:] From which follows the phonological relevance of the acute and the grave (but only on monosyllables): phonetically the acute possibly denoted a short rising tone, and the grave a short falling one (Oslon 2012: 74). ... [fn. 2:] This concerns dialects that distinguish these tones phonologically (Križanić did not distinguish them — he has only one phonologically relevant long tone, see below).

tone_statements.summary: Križanić's 17th-c. Čakavian-based idiom, from his accent marks: three prosodemes, two short accents (contrast only in monosyllables; rising vs falling tentative) and one long; long neo-acute lost as a prosodeme. Free paradigmatic accent place presupposed. On Kajkavian proper: 'three-accent systems'.

tone_statements.citation: Beguš, Gašper. 2015. The Circumflex Advancement in Prekmurje Slovenian and Bednja Kajkavian. Zeitschrift für Slawistik 60(1): 33-44.
tone_statements.quote: Kao i u većini drugih kajkavskih troakcenatskih govorā, kratki naglasak u govoru Svetoga Đurđa ne ostvaruje se nužno kao silazni, već se može realizirati i kao tromi ( ʺ ), budući da intonacija u kratkome slogu nije fonološki relevantna kao u standardnome hrvatskom jeziku ili u novoštokavskim, četveroakcenatskim sustavima. ... zadržao bih se na Ivšićevu zaključku koji ovaj govor smješta u tip I5, odnosno, Lončarićevoj tvrdnji ... da se radi o troakcenatskom sustavu koji čine kratki naglasak, dugosilazni naglasak te akut.
tone_statements.translation: As in most other Kajkavian three-accent dialects, the short accent in the Sveti Đurđ dialect is not necessarily realised as falling but may also be realised as 'slow' ( ʺ ), since intonation in a short syllable is not phonologically relevant as it is in standard Croatian or in Neo-Štokavian four-accent systems. ... I would stay with Ivšić's conclusion placing this dialect in type I5, i.e. Lončarić's claim ... that it is a three-accent system consisting of the short accent, the long falling accent and the acute.
tone_statements.locator: p. 92, 2.2.2 Realizacija naglasaka; then pp. 94-95, 2.2.7 Umjesto zaključka o akcentuaciji
tone_statements.summary: Three accents: short, long rising (akut), long falling; pitch contrasts only on long accented syllables. Fieldwork, 40 minimal pairs differing only in intonation (Table 2, e.g. dȋm ~ dĩm), refutes Lončarić/Belović-Blažeka's view that only an earlier reading place matters. Pretonic length lost; 140+ forms.

tone_statements.citation: Kapović, Mate. 2015. Povijest hrvatske akcentuacije: Fonetika [History of Croatian accentuation: Phonetics]. Zagreb: Matica hrvatska. 1046 pp. ISBN 978-953-150-971-8. (Review: Mandić, David. 2016. Croatica et Slavica Iadertina 12(2): 631-634, Hrčak ID 178586.)
tone_statements.quote: Inventar prozodema čine tri naglaska – dva duga (silazni i uzlazni) i kratki ( ̑ , ˜ , ˈ ) – te nenaglašena kračina. ... Realizacija – Kratki se naglasak ˈ ostvaruje većinom silazno. – Dugi se uzlazni naglasak ˜ ostvaruje većinom ravno ili blago uzlazno. ... Govor je tronaglasan. Postoji dvostruki naglasak: na mjestu ishodišne prednaglasne dužine u antepenultimi dugi je silazni naglasak, uz čuvanje kratkoga naglaska na ishodišno naglašenoj penultimi, te na mjestu ishodišne prednaglasne dužine na penultimi ispred dugoga silaznoga naglaska na ultimi.
tone_statements.translation: The inventory of prosodemes consists of three accents – two long (falling and rising) and a short one ( ̑ , ˜ , ˈ ) – plus unaccented shortness. ... Realisation – The short accent ˈ is realised mostly as falling. – The long rising accent ˜ is realised mostly level or slightly rising. ... The dialect has three accents. There is a double accent: in place of the original pretonic length on the antepenult there is a long falling accent, with the short accent kept on the originally accented penult, and in place of original pretonic length on the penult before a long falling accent on the ultima.
tone_statements.locator: p. 174, sec. 3.1 Prozodija 'Inventar'; p. 175 'Realizacija'; p. 190, sec. 4 Zaključak
tone_statements.summary: Three-accent Kajkavian system (long falling, long rising, short), no unaccented length; original pretonic length analysed as a second long falling accent, giving double-accented words (pȋsti); fn. 8: others treat it as pretonic length. 60+ accented forms in 3.1.

tone_statements.citation: Horvat, Joža. 2011. Prozodija i vokalizam govora Svetoga Đurđa [Prosody and vocalism of the local dialect of Sveti Đurđ]. Hrvatski dijalektološki zbornik 17: 81-107.
tone_statements.quote: Najstariji je naglasni sustav i štok. i čak. i kajk. onaj s 3 naglaska ( ̏, ̑, ˜) i prednaglasnim i zanaglasnim duljinama (osim kajk. koji, dakako, nema zanaglasnih duljina). Sva su tri naglaska mogla stajati na bilo kojem slogu, a prednaglasna se duljina izvorno nalazila samo neposredno ispred dočetnoga ̏. ... Često se napominje kako u čak. i kajk. tronaglasnim sustavima, gdje nema kratkoga uzlaznoga naglaska, ̏ ne mora nužno biti fonetski silazan.
tone_statements.translation: The oldest accentual system of Štokavian, Čakavian and Kajkavian alike is the one with 3 accents ( ̏ [short falling], ̑ [long falling], ˜ [neoacute]) and pretonic and posttonic lengths (except Kajkavian, which of course has no posttonic lengths). All three accents could stand on any syllable, and pretonic length was originally found only immediately before a final ̏. ... It is often remarked that in Čakavian and Kajkavian three-accent systems, where there is no short rising accent, ̏ need not be phonetically falling.
tone_statements.locator: p. 27, section 'Najstariji hrvatski naglasni sustavi i prednaglasna duljina'; sentence after '..' = p. 10, footnote 25
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Archaic Kajkavian: free 3-accent pitch accent system (short falling, long falling, neoacute), pretonic but no posttonic length; short falling mostly long-drawn ('tromi'), in Zabok may merge with neoacute; some dialects merge neoacute into long falling (p. 28); Podravina restricts accent place.

tone_statements.citation: Kapović, Mate. 2009. Čakavsko i kajkavsko u donjosutlanskoj akcentuaciji (na primjeru govora Drinja) [Čakavian and Kajkavian features in the accentuation of the Lower Sutla dialect of Drinje]. Hrvatski dijalektološki zbornik 15: 195-209.
tone_statements.quote: Nakon navedenih prozodijskih inovacija dobivena je osnovna kajkavska akcentuacija, „troakcenatska”: tri naglaska (prozodema sa silinom), s nenaglašenom duljinom u slogovima ispred naglaska (prednaglasna duljina). Akcenti su: jedan kratki (netonem) i dva duga: cirkumfleks – dugosilazni i akut – dugouzlazni te nenaglašena duljina i kračina. OKA dakle ima pet prozodema. Svi prozodemi osim nenaglašene duljine mogu doći na svakome mjestu u riječi, i u zadnjem i u jedinom slogu.
tone_statements.translation: After the prosodic innovations listed, the basic Kajkavian accentuation was obtained, a 'three-accent' one: three accents (prosodemes with stress), with unstressed length in syllables before the accent (pretonic length). The accents are: one short (a non-toneme) and two long: the circumflex – long falling, and the acute – long rising, plus unstressed length and shortness. OKA thus has five prosodemes. All prosodemes except unstressed length can occur in any position in the word, including the final and the only syllable.
tone_statements.summary: Historical review: basic Kajkavian accentuation = 3 accents (short, no tonal contrast; long falling circumflex; long rising acute) plus pretonic length, free in position; Međimurje and W Zagorje/upper Sutla dialects lost the tonal opposition, then quantity (p. 191). 60+ accented forms pp. 191-197.

tone_statements.citation: Kapović, Mate. 2008. Razvoj hrvatske akcentuacije [The development of Croatian accentuation]. Filologija 51: 1-39. Zagreb: HAZU. Hrčak ID 33802; open PDFhttps://hrcak.srce.hr/file/53755.
tone_statements.quote: …i nakon male sumnje za mene je postalo potpuno jasno da ta valpovačka akcentucija ima dva dugosilazna akcenta. Prvi je onaj isti koji imamo i u književnom govoru, a koji se nalazi u riječima kao grȃd, prȃvda, lȃđica itd. … Moje je međutim duboko uvjerenje da taj akcenat pada kudikamo dublje, nego književni dugosilazni, a osim toga ja osjećam i neki lagani prizvuk na posljednjem slogu, otprilike kao pȋšȉ, što je razumljivo, jer dolazi od pīšȉ… Ja sam za ovakav akcenat uzeo dva znaka…
tone_statements.translation: …and after slight doubt it became completely clear to me that this Valpovo accentuation has two long-falling accents. The first is the same one we have in the literary language, found in words like grȃd, prȃvda, lȃđica etc. … It is however my deep conviction that that [second] accent falls far deeper than the literary long-falling one, and besides I also perceive a slight after-tone on the last syllable, roughly like pȋšȉ, which is understandable since it comes from pīšȉ… For this accent I adopted two signs…

tone_statements.summary: Reply to Hamm on the Slavonian Štokavian-Ekavian Valpovo (lower Podravina) accentuation, not Kajkavian: in the Serbo-Croatian pitch accent frame Klaić posits two distinct long-falling accents plus post-accentual lengths; no full inventory. 'akcentucija' sic; accent marks read from a 150-dpi image.

tone_statements.citation: Lončarić, Mijo. 1982. Prilog podjeli kajkavskoga narječja [A contribution to the classification of the Kajkavian dialect group]. Hrvatski dijalektološki zbornik 6: 237-245. Zagreb: JAZU. (Hrčak ID 204502)
tone_statements.quote: The distinctive features in the accentuation of Blatnica Pokupska are stress, length and tone. Unstressed vowels are either short or, in rare examples, long. ... Stress can fall on any syllable of the word, except on a short final syllable (see below). ... Stressed syllables are either long or short, and a distinction in tone can be made in long stressed syllables only. The accent system therefore consists of four units, one of which is extremely rare: /ȁ, ȃ, ã, (ā)/
tone_statements.summary: Kajkavian word accent with distinctive stress place, length and tone; rising vs falling tone only on long stressed syllables; four units /ȁ ȃ ã (ā)/, the last rare pretonic length; length and pitch distinctions tend to neutralize (esp. finally), eroding the three-unit system. Fieldwork 2008-09.

tone_statements.citation: Lončarić, Mijo. 1977. Jagnjedovački govor (s osvrtom na pitanje kajkavskoga podravskog dijalekta) [The dialect of Jagnjedovac, with reference to the question of the Kajkavian Podravina dialect]. Hrvatski dijalektološki zbornik 4: 179-262. Zagreb: JAZU.
tone_statements.quote: Der Dialekt von Virje kennt auch drei Akzente, aber drei nur nach der Quantität, d. i. kurzen, mittellangen und langen. Nach der Tonqualität können wir weder in langen und noch weniger in mittellangen und kurzen Silben steigende Intonation konstatieren, sondern nur fallende (oder wenigstens keine steigende). ... Hier können wir gleich erwähnen, daß dieser Dialekt die Unterscheidung verschiedener Formen durch verschiedene Tonqualität aufgegeben und die Unterscheidung durch verschiedene Quantität vorgezogen hat
tone_statements.translation: The dialect of Virje also has three accents, but three only by quantity, i.e. short, mid-long and long. As to tone quality we can establish rising intonation neither in long nor, still less, in mid-long and short syllables, but only falling (or at least no rising). ... Here we may mention at once that this dialect has given up distinguishing different forms by different tone quality and preferred distinction by different quantity
tone_statements.locator: p. 347 and p. 350, section III c Silbenakzent
tone_statements.summary: Virje Kajkavian: no rising/falling accent contrast; its three accents (short ̏, mid-long ̀, long ̑) differ only in quantity, all falling or plain an earlier reading; forms kept apart by quantity or accent place, not tone quality (p. 358). Checked by ear with Rešetar and a native speaker's musical notation.

tone_statements.citation: Jedvaj, Josip. 1956. Bednjanski govor [The dialect of Bednja]. Hrvatski dijalektološki zbornik 1: 279-330. Zagreb: JAZU.
tone_statements.quote: Govor Drinja ima tronaglasni sustav ( ̏ , ̑ , ͂ ) s prednaglasnom duljinom ( ̄ ), koja dolazi samo ispred naglaska ̏. Kao što je rečeno, u govoru nije bilo nikakvih fonetskih povlačenja naglasaka, tj. svi su naglasci očuvali svoja stara mjesta, npr. nogȁ, glāvȁ, G. nogẽ itd. ̏ se ostvaruje tipično kajkavski, katkada posve kratko ..., ali se umjesto njega često javlja i aloton ˝, tj. “tromi” naglasak (fonetski poludug ili dug). ... Naglasak je ̑ , tipično za kajkavski i čakavski, nešto kraći od štokavskoga ̑ . Neoakut ͂ je uglavnom poprilično stabilan u neposljednjim slogovima...
tone_statements.translation: The dialect of Drinje has a three-accent system ( ̏ , ̑ , ͂ ) with pretonic length ( ̄ ), which occurs only before the accent ̏. As said, there were no phonetic accent retractions in the dialect, i.e. all accents kept their old places, e.g. nogȁ, glāvȁ, G. nogẽ etc. ̏ is realised in the typical Kajkavian way, sometimes quite short ..., but instead of it the allotone ˝, i.e. the 'sluggish' accent (phonetically half-long or long), often appears. ... The accent ̑ is, typically for Kajkavian and Čakavian, somewhat shorter than Štokavian ̑. The neoacute ͂ is on the whole fairly stable in non-final syllables...
tone_statements.summary: Three-accent system (double grave = short falling, circumflex = long falling, neoacute; standard Croatian dialectological symbols) plus pretonic length; accent place free, unretracted (nogȁ, glāvȁ). Pitch shapes not described; author's fieldwork; instrumental study still needed. 200+ accented forms.

tone_statements.citation: Klaić, A[dolf]. 1936. O podravskom akcentu i kvantitetu [On the Podravina accent and quantity]. Južnoslovenski filolog 15: 181-183. Beograd: Srpska (kraljevska) akademija. Open PDF:https://dais.sanu.ac.rs/bitstream/id/28953/klaic.podravski.1936.pdf(685 KB).
tone_statements.quote: Leaving aside for the moment the various combinations of the grapheme y with diacritics, we can say that the place of the stress (which is distinctive) is indicated by means of ‶, ⁀ or ˜. Length is implied by ⁀, ˜ or ˉ, shortness by ‶ or the absence of any diacritic. ... There is a pitch opposition on long vowels and diphthongs in stressed syllables; ⁀ denotes the falling pitch, ˜ the rising pitch.

tone_statements.quote: Akcenta su tri: ̏ (kratki), ̑ (dugi silazni) i ~ (akut, dugi uzlazni). Dugi slogovi izvan akcenta (označeni znakom –) nalaze se samo ispred naglašenih slogova. Kratki je akcenat iza dugoga sloga uvijek ekspiratoričan, a inače je intonacioni. Tako je na pr. razlika u izgovoru naglašenoga i u riječi kēyrȉti (kuriti) (izgovor je vrlo kratak i odsječen) i sȉlo (izgovor je nešto dulji i naginje na akut). Na diftonzima silazni se akcenat izgovara, kao da je prvi dio diftonga naglašen brzim akcentom, pa s njega sila izgovora silazi u padanju na drugi dio, koji mnogo slabije dolazi do izražaja.
tone_statements.translation: There are three accents: ̏ (short), ̑ (long falling) and ~ (acute, long rising). Long syllables outside the accent (marked with –) occur only before accented syllables. The short accent after a long syllable is always expiratory, otherwise it is tonal (intonational). Thus e.g. the difference in the pronunciation of accented i in kēyrȉti 'kuriti' (very short and clipped) and sȉlo (somewhat longer, tending towards the acute). On diphthongs the falling accent is pronounced as if the first part of the diphthong were stressed with the quick accent, and from it the force of pronunciation descends, falling, onto the second part, which is much less prominent.

tone.translation: The dialect of Virje also has three accents, but three only by quantity, i.e. short, mid-long and long. As to tone quality we can establish rising intonation neither in long nor, still less, in mid-long and short syllables, but only falling (or at least no rising). ... Here we may mention at once that this dialect has given up distinguishing different forms by different tone quality and preferred distinction by different quantity

tone.translation: The dialect of Drinje has a three-accent system ( ̏ , ̑ , ͂ ) with pretonic length ( ̄ ), which occurs only before the accent ̏. As said, there were no phonetic accent retractions in the dialect, i.e. all accents kept their old places, e.g. nogȁ, glāvȁ, G. nogẽ etc. ̏ is realised in the typical Kajkavian way, sometimes quite short ..., but instead of it the allotone ˝, i.e. the 'sluggish' accent (phonetically half-long or long), often appears. ... The accent ̑ is, typically for Kajkavian and Čakavian, somewhat shorter than Štokavian ̑. The neoacute ͂ is on the whole fairly stable in non-final syllables...

tone.translation: After the prosodic innovations listed, the basic Kajkavian accentuation was obtained, a 'three-accent' one: three accents (prosodemes with stress), with unstressed length in syllables before the accent (pretonic length). The accents are: one short (a non-toneme) and two long: the circumflex – long falling, and the acute – long rising, plus unstressed length and shortness. OKA thus has five prosodemes. All prosodemes except unstressed length can occur in any position in the word, including the final and the only syllable.

sources.quote: The distinctive features in the accentuation of Blatnica Pokupska are stress, length and tone. Unstressed vowels are either short or, in rare examples, long. ... Stress can fall on any syllable of the word, except on a short final syllable (see below). ... Stressed syllables are either long or short, and a distinction in tone can be made in long stressed syllables only. The accent system therefore consists of four units, one of which is extremely rare: /ȁ, ȃ, ã, (ā)/
sources.note: Kajkavian word accent with distinctive stress place, length and tone; rising vs falling tone only on long stressed syllables; four units /ȁ ȃ ã (ā)/, the last rare pretonic length; length and pitch distinctions tend to neutralize (esp. finally), eroding the three-unit system. Fieldwork 2008-09.

Although it is not entirely clear how the original word was accented, the long falling tone on the second syllable in Bednja strongly suggests that it had a circumflex on the first syllable. ... It is true that in Bednja, the ictus remains on the final syllable, but the preceding vowel gets lengthened and the length has a falling pitch. This length is thus very similar to the length of the original circumflex, e.g. yēby̏l for PSl. *ob-bűlъ or nāōpȉt vs. nȃobrol.
